name: Test and improve your soil
blurb: Everything in gardening rests on soil. Ten minutes of testing tells you what you are working with and saves years of blaming the plants.
gear: Organic matter: compost, leaf mould or well-rotted manure
steps: Do the jar test for texture: soil and water in a jar, shaken and left to settle into sand, silt and clay layers.
Test the pH, which determines what nutrients plants can actually take up. Most vegetables want roughly 6.5.
Dig a hole and look: is it compacted, does water sit in it, are there worms? Worm count is a fast proxy for soil health.
Add organic matter as a mulch on the surface rather than digging it in — the soil life will incorporate it for you.
Stop walking on beds. Compaction is the most common and most invisible soil problem.
Keep the soil covered, with plants or mulch, year round.
tips: Adding lime or sulphur to change pH is slow and easy to overdo. Test first, adjust gradually.
A "feed the soil, not the plant" approach outperforms fertiliser over a few seasons.
proof: You can state your soil’s texture and pH, and show visible improvement after a season of mulching.
